extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing literary fiction writers, especially short-story writers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing dense, timeless literary short stories that function as intellectual hypotheses, emphasizing clarity, inevitability of phrasing, and certain recurring devices associated with Borges' aesthetics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity and compressed form (density over length)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The short story can be taken in at a single glance" while novels depend on "padding, on pages which are mere nexuses." Borges famously preferred the story to the novel and is the great defender of compressed fiction. Density should achieve what novelistic length attempts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer compression: make the short story achieve novel-like richness without padding. Avoid extraneous pages or sections that exist only to fill space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction as an intellectual hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: "Fiction is based on the examination of an intellectual possibility presented as a narrative hypothesis." A story is a thought experiment dressed as event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct stories around a clear intellectual possibility or conceptual question and explore it through narrative action rather than merely reporting events; the premise should function like a hypothesis being examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refinement through tradition (folk-tale economy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Folk tales are "a much more refined product" than authored verse because they have "been stripped of everything that might be useless or bothersome" through generations of retelling. Communal editing yields perfection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value economy and elimination of the superfluous. Consider how traditional, pared-down forms accomplish clarity and potency by removing what is unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid contemporary specificity (timeless/indeterminate setting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set stories "in somewhat indeterminate places and many years ago" to avoid readers scrutinizing factual accuracy. Abstraction protects artistic integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor indeterminate or non-specific settings and temporal markers so readers focus on the idea and form rather than checking historical or geographical facts; this abstraction helps achieve universality and reduces distractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use simple words; avoid self-attention-grabbing diction
rubrics_metrics.description: - Use simple words; avoid the word that calls attention to itself
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose language that feels inevitable and unobtrusive; avoid flashy or showy words whose presence draws attention away from the idea or narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metaphors must connect genuinely related things
rubrics_metrics.description: - Distrust the metaphor that surprises only by novelty — use only metaphors that connect things genuinely linked
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid novelty-for-its-own-sake metaphors. A good metaphor should reveal a genuine, intelligible connection between the things it links rather than startling the reader merely through unexpectedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inevitability of word choice
rubrics_metrics.description: "I would like to write in such a way that the reader thinks the words are inevitable"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for phrasing and diction that feel unavoidable and perfectly apt; readers should feel the wording is the only possible way to express what is being conveyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not be original at the cost of clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: - Do not be original at the cost of clarity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize clear communication over forced originality or novelty. Originality that obscures meaning is undesirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity over literary schools (individual voice)
rubrics_metrics.description: "I no longer believe in literary schools now; I believe in the individual."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate the individual writer's voice rather than writing to conform to a current school or fashion; authenticity is more valuable than adherence to literary trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing as play (joyful process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative work "doesn't feel it to be a chore; one feels it to be a form of amusement." The writer who works grimly produces dead text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach writing with a spirit of play and amusement; a grim, joyless attitude tends to produce lifeless prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring structural devices (Borgesian motifs)
rubrics_metrics.description:
- The labyrinth (literal and metaphorical)
- The infinite library
- Doubling and the doppelgänger
- The unreliable scholar / fictional bibliography
- The story-within-a-story
- The dream that contains the dreamer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are characteristic structural and thematic devices Borges employs; consider using motifs like labyrinths, doubling, embedded texts, and mise-en-abyme to structure intellectual/ metaphysical stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelessness / transcending historical moment
rubrics_metrics.description: A truly timeless book "would be just as admirable if it had been published a hundred years before or if it were published a hundred years later."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for qualities that allow a story to transcend its immediate historical context—avoid over-anchoring to contemporary detail so the work can be appreciated across eras.
